name: USS Nimitz “Tic Tac” Encounter
blurb: Navy F/A-18 pilots and the Nimitz strike group tracked a 40-foot wingless “Tic Tac” on radar and gun-camera. One of the best-sensored military cases on record.

name: Area 51 / S-4
blurb: Bob Lazar claimed he reverse-engineered alien craft at a site south of Groom Lake. The physics is intriguing; the corroboration is thin.

name: Roswell Incident
blurb: Debris on a ranch, a press release that said “flying disc,” then a hasty walk-back to “weather balloon.” The founding myth of modern ufology.

name: The Phoenix Lights
blurb: Thousands watched a silent V-formation of lights cross Arizona. Flares explain part of it; the earlier craft sightings less so.

name: Rendlesham Forest
blurb: USAF personnel near RAF Woodbridge reported a landed craft and radiation traces. Britain’s most documented military case.

name: The Belgian Wave
blurb: Months of triangular-craft reports, backed by police witnesses and an F-16 radar-lock chase the Belgian Air Force openly investigated.

name: Washington D.C. Flap
blurb: Unknowns painted on radar over the capital two weekends running, prompting jet intercepts and a hurried Air Force press conference.

name: Kecksburg UFO
blurb: A fireball, then reports of an acorn-shaped object recovered by the military. Officially a meteor; locally, something else.

name: Westall School Sighting
blurb: Some 200 students and staff watched a craft descend near their school. One of the largest mass sightings on record.

name: Tehran Dogfight
blurb: Two Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4s scrambled on an object that reportedly knocked out their instruments and weapons. Documented in a US DIA memo.

name: Japan Air Lines Flight 1628
blurb: A JAL cargo 747 crew tracked enormous craft over Alaska for nearly an hour. The FAA investigated and never fully explained it.

name: Trans-en-Provence Case
blurb: A farmer reported a landed disc; France’s GEPAN found unusual soil and plant changes at the site. A rare physical-trace investigation.

name: Trindade Island Photos
blurb: A Brazilian Navy expedition photographed a Saturn-shaped object. The negatives were vouched for by the government of the day.

name: Hudson Valley Sightings
blurb: Years of huge, silent boomerang-craft reports across the New York–Connecticut border. Some, but not all, tied to hoaxing pilots.

name: Stephenville Lights
blurb: Dozens of residents, including a pilot, reported a mile-wide craft. FAA radar data later showed unexplained tracks in the area.

name: Aguadilla Thermal Video
blurb: A Customs and Border Protection aircraft filmed an object skimming the sea and apparently splitting in two on infrared.

name: O’Hare Airport Sighting
blurb: United Airlines staff reported a disc hovering over Gate C17 before it shot upward, punching a hole in the cloud deck.

name: Levelland Vehicle Interference
blurb: A dozen drivers independently reported an egg-shaped object that stalled their engines and headlights, then departed.

name: Shag Harbour Incident
blurb: Something crashed into the harbour and sank; the RCMP and Navy searched. Canada’s files list it as an unsolved UFO case.

name: Varginha Case
blurb: Locals claimed the military captured a strange creature. Enormously popular in Brazil, thin on hard evidence.

name: Ariel School Encounter
blurb: Around 60 schoolchildren described a landed craft and beings, telling remarkably consistent stories to investigators.

name: Malmstrom Missile Shutdown
blurb: Officers reported a craft over the base as a flight of Minuteman ICBMs dropped offline. Corroborated by multiple missileers.

name: Cash–Landrum Incident
blurb: Two women reported a diamond-shaped craft escorted by helicopters, then suffered burns and radiation-like illness.

name: Kenneth Arnold / Mount Rainier
blurb: A pilot reported nine fast, flat, crescent-shaped objects racing along the Cascades. His skipping-saucer simile coined the term 'flying saucer' and launched the modern UFO era.
